newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey ups tax on wheat, corn seed oil imports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey ups tax on wheat, corn seed oil imports.

text.p: Turkey on Saturday raised taxes on imports of non-seed wheat, non-seed corn and two types of sunflower seed oil as well as raising tax and imposing levies on imports of several meat and meat products, the Official Gazette said in a government decree.

The decree, which took immediate effect, said import tax on non-seed wheat imports was raised to 15 percent from three. The import tax on non-seed corn imports was also raised to 15 percent from three.
The government raised import taxes on two types of sunflower seed oil which it did not identify to 50 percent and 39 percent from 24 and 12 percent, respectively.

Taxes on imports of several meat types and meat products were increased up to 105 percent from a range between 15 percent to 95 percent. Imports of such products were also levied up to $60 per tonne on the cost-insurance-and-freight (CIF) price of each product, the decree said.
Turkish agriculture ministry officials earlier mentioned the increase in taxes which they said had been planned following a higher domestic wheat and corn crop.

Turkey expects to produce 19 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97, up from 15.5 million tonnes last year, but Western trade reports said it could not produce more than 16.5 million tonnes this crop year.
Farm officials said Turkey's private companies had imported about 800,000 tonnes of wheat so far in 1996.
Pasta producers, who say Turkish durum wheat quality is not satisfactory, have said they will carry out durum imports regardless of the raise in customs tax.
A farm official said on Friday the corn import tax raise was considered because the country's corn output would rise up to 2.2 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 1.8 million in the previous year.
"With a good harvest like that, we cannot let cheaper imported corn enter the market," he said.
Subsidised purchases of corn by the Turkish Grain Board (TMO), the government agent which buys grain from farmers, are made at about $195.5 per tonne, compared to world prices of about $145.
Corn traders said the industries using non-seed corn in Turkey, which they say imports up to 900,000 tonnes every year, would be adversely affected from raised import taxes.

Agricultural officials earlier said customs taxes and levies were needed for meat and meat products to stop imports because of concerns of several livestock diseases in origin countries, mainly those in the Middle East and Balkans.
Turkey also expects a higher sunflower seed harvest this year, but no production figures have been made available by the government yet.
